post.instagram_caption:
In 1913, a roulette wheel in Monte Carlo landed on black 26 times in a row.

Gamblers were sure red was due and lost millions of francs betting against black. The wheel has no memory, so every spin is a fresh chance. That mistake is called the gambler's fallacy.
